reading: The input is the left half of a symmetric outline; mirror it about the vertical axis just right of its rightmost column, then output only the enclosed interior filled with the outline colour (the outline itself is erased).
verb: complete by mirror and fill interior

slots.half: the single fg object (left half of an outline)
slots.fill: background cells enclosed by the mirrored outline, painted the outline colour

why: output cells are exactly the bg cells strictly inside the mirrored closed outline, in its colour

reading: A 5 pivot has an arm of 2s; the arm is rotated 90 degrees clockwise about the pivot (new arm in 2), and the old arm cells become 3.

slots.arm: the straight run of 2s touching the pivot
slots.rotation: 90 degrees clockwise about the pivot, same length, colour 2

why: new 2 cells are the old arm rotated clockwise about the 5; old arm cells are 3

reading: Each hollow square of 5s has its interior filled with a colour set by the interior size: 1x1 -> 6, 2x2 -> 7, 3x3 -> 8.
why: every interior cell gets the colour keyed by its square's interior side; outlines unchanged

reading: A 1xN row with a 2 in the middle becomes an NxN grid: the 2 spreads as a V of two diagonals down to the sides, and diagonal lines of 1 parallel to the right arm (every 4 columns) are drawn below the left arm.
verb: draw diagonal V and parallel rays

slots.size: N x N where N is input width
slots.V: 2 diagonals from the top centre down-left and down-right to the edges
slots.rays: 1-coloured down-right diagonals with X-Y = (right arm X-Y) - 4k, k>=1, drawn only below the left arm

why: row 0 is the input; 2s on both diagonals from the centre; 1s on the spaced parallel diagonals below the left arm

reading: Every full row or column made only of 0 (a non-background colour here) is recoloured to 2.

new_rows.name: fullline
new_rows.datalog:
rowlen(Y, count(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rowc(Y, C, count(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
fullrow(Y, C) :- rowc(Y, C, N), rowlen(Y, M), N = M.
collen(X, count(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
colc(X, C, count(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
fullcol(X, C) :- colc(X, C, N), collen(X, M), N = M.
fullline(Y, X) :- fullrow(Y, C), cell(Y, X, C).
fullline(Y, X) :- fullcol(X, C), cell(Y, X, C).

why: cells on a full single-colour non-background line change 0 -> 2; nothing else changes

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled 3x3; a block gets a copy of the input where the input cell has the most common colour, other blocks are empty.
why: block (i,j) is the input iff input[i][j] is the most common (background) colour, else all 0

reading: Full background columns split the grid into panels, each with one pattern colour; background cells in each panel take the colour of the next panel to the right (the last wraps to the first).
verb: recolour panel background by next panel

slots.panels: column stripes between full background-colour columns
slots.subject: background cells inside each panel
slots.colour: the pattern colour of the next panel to the right, cyclic

why: in panel i every bg cell becomes colour(panel i+1 mod n); separator columns and pattern cells unchanged

reading: Each 1-coloured segment on a grid edge points at the hollow square aligned with it; that square is repeated with period equal to its size toward that edge (cut at the border), and the 1 segment is removed.

slots.markers: 1-coloured segments on the grid border, same length as a square side
slots.subject: the square sharing the marker's rows (left/right edge) or columns (top/bottom edge)
slots.repeat: copies of the square every side-length cells toward the marker's edge, truncated at the border

why: output = squares plus periodic copies from each square to its marker edge; no 1 remains

reading: Some rectangles have a one-cell-wide tail; each such rectangle slides in the tail's direction by the tail's length and the tail disappears; rectangles it was covering are shown whole, and the moved rectangle is drawn on top.

slots.subject: rectangles with a protruding 1-wide tail
slots.rest: tail removed; occluded rectangles completed to full boxes; moved rectangle drawn on top

why: each tailed rectangle appears shifted by its tail vector, untailed rectangles appear as full boxes

reading: The input is tiled 3x3; then on the big grid, every row containing a coloured cell is filled with 1 (except the coloured cells), and each coloured cell gets a 3 at its up-left and down-right diagonal neighbours.

slots.line: row through each coloured cell, background cells -> 1
slots.diagonals: cells at (-1,-1) and (+1,+1) of each coloured cell -> 3 (inside grid)

why: output is 3x3 tiling of input with 1-rows through coloured cells and 3s on their NW/SE diagonals
invariants: coloured input cells in every tile
